title.narrative: [THEME 1 and 2] Integrated Lifesaving Humanitarian Assistance for People Affected by Critical Malnutrition and Gender-Based Violence in Gumi Eldelo Woreda, Oromia Region

description.narrative: ltpgtThis integrated, multisectoral emergency response project targets conflict and climate-affected populations in Gumi Eldelo woredas of East Borena Zone, Oromia Region. These are areas marked by high food insecurity, limited WASH access, poor nutrition indicators, protection risks, and underfunded humanitarian interventions. Informed by a May 2025 joint multi-sectoral needs assessment conducted by Mercy Corps and ANE, and validated through community consultations and sectoral data, the project aims to provide lifesaving, protection-sensitive, and inclusive assistance to 49,558 individuals across five sectors: Nutrition, Health, WASH, Agriculture and Protection (GBV-focused). ltbrgtUnder Health and Nutrition, the project will deploy mobile outreach teams to provide Integrated Management of Acute Malnutrition (IMAM) services for children under-five and pregnant and lactating women (PLW), including nutrition screening, referrals, and micronutrient supplementation. Community health workers will conduct home visits, complemented by visual materials for awareness raising. Nutrition-sensitive messaging will be integrated with other sectoral activities, particularly agriculture and WASH. ltbrgtThe WASH activities will address critical gaps in safe water access and hygiene promotion. Activities include the rehabilitation of 7 water schemes, distribution of hygiene kits (with menstrual health supplies), and community-led hygiene behavior change campaigns, all tailored to the target communities and women, girls, and persons with disabilities. WASH committees will be formed or revitalized and trained to manage infrastructure sustainably. ltbrgtIn Agriculture, the intervention will safeguard agro-pastoral livelihoods by distributing poultry starter kits, including vaccinated chicks and basic equipment, to 7,924 vulnerable individuals, including women and adolescent girls, paired with vouchers redeemable from local vendors to stimulate local market activity. The project promotes gender-responsive livelihoods by linking poultry production to income generation and nutrition outcomes, reinforced by technical training and follow-up. ltbrgtThe Protection component prioritizes GBV prevention, mitigation, and response. It will establish one Women and Girls Safe Space offering psychosocial support and empowerment activities for 580 women and girls. GBV case management will be delivered to 40 survivors by trained case workers, linked to medical, legal, and psychosocial services. Community dialogues with men, youth, and leaders will address harmful gender norms, while referral pathways will be strengthened in collaboration with Women’s and Children’s Affairs Bureau, OSCs, and the Protection Cluster. Survivors will receive cash for protection, while all community members will benefit from confidential PSEA channels, monitored through Mercy Corps’ Responsible Data Policy. ltbrgtTo ensure effective and safe implementation, the consortium will leverage existing field teams, surge rosters, and prepositioned supplies. A regional MEL and CARM specialists will manage MEL activities and track SMART indicators disaggregated by sex, age, and disability. Data will be collected bi-monthly, feeding into adaptive management and regular reporting to clusters and OCHA. ltbrgtThe project ensures accountability to affected populations through Community Accountability Reporting Mechanisms, inclusive planning processes, and regular feedback mechanisms tailored to marginalized groups. Gender equality and disability inclusion are mainstreamed, with targeted investments in GBV response, protection, and livelihood support for women and girls. ltbrgtThis 12-month intervention aligns with the 2025 HRP, contributing to HRP Strategic Objectives. It complements ongoing CBPF and CERF efforts in Oromia, targeting underserved kebeles and filling sectoral gaps through coordinated, community-driven programming that strengthens local ownership and promotes durable solutions. ltbrgtlt/pgt
